clue.text: Don't notice one going off alone with a book

indicators.note: something going off departs, so the named word leaves the longer word it sits in

blocks.note: to fail to notice something is to miss it
taken as written, the part that leaves
taken as written, the word it leaves

explanation.surface: Someone sits alone with a book, oblivious to a person leaving the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going off alone' reads as a lonely person leaving, but it is an instruction to remove a word from inside the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the Catholic service book containing the texts for celebrating Mass through the year.

clue.text: You won't have to search for them high and low on the map

definitions.text: You won't have to search for them high and low on the map

blocks.clueFragment: You won't have to search for them high and low
blocks.note: surface reading: things easy to find, no exhaustive hunt needed

blocks.clueFragment: high and low on the map
blocks.note: setter's reading: regions neither at the top nor bottom of a map, but in its centre

explanation.walkthrough: 'High and low' sounds like the idiom for searching everywhere, but on a map it means north and south; these lands sit in between.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midlands are the central counties of England, lying between the north and the south on any map of the country.

clue.text: Unusual in not having an S on the end?

definitions.text: not having an S on the end

blocks.note: first meaning: remarkable, out of the ordinary

blocks.clueFragment: not having an S on the end
blocks.note: second meaning: the grammatical number of a noun with no plural ending

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about a word that oddly lacks its final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Most English plurals end in S, so a noun without one is usually in the grammatical form for one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means both strikingly odd and, in grammar, the form naming one thing rather than several.

clue.text: The friends got sea sick in turn

indicators.note: the first word has obtained or taken in the second, so one goes inside the other
turned around, the combined letters are read from the end back to the start

blocks.note: taken as written
to be sick is to be ill

explanation.surface: A group of companions all became seasick one after another on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA takes in ILL to make SEILLA, which read backwards gives ALLIES. The answer stands without 'The', which only fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are partners or supporters who stand together, so they are close companions in a common cause.

clue.text: Agreed I can tie up with string

indicators.note: to tie something up is to knot and twist it, so these letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
cord is thin string

explanation.surface: Someone offers to secure a parcel with a length of string.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord means being in agreement, so parties who have agreed are of one mind on a matter.

clue.text: French you and I savvy

blocks.note: first meaning: the French pronoun for 'we'
second meaning: practical common sense

explanation.surface: A boast that the speaker and a French friend are both shrewd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You and I' together make 'we', which in French is the same word as the English noun for good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is informal British English for practical intelligence and shrewdness, which is what savvy means as a noun.

clue.text: Needs but doesn't expect to have delivered

blocks.note: first meaning: requires or demands
second meaning: goes to collect an item in person

explanation.surface: A shopper who requires something but plans to fetch it rather than have it sent.
explanation.walkthrough: To call for a parcel is to go round and pick it up, the opposite of waiting for delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation that requires something demands it; separately, someone collecting goods in person goes round to fetch them.

clue.text: Key member of the cricket team?

blocks.note: first meaning: a device that unlocks something
second meaning: one of the two batsmen who start an innings

explanation.surface: A question about who is the most important player in a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as an adjective meaning important, but it is a noun: a tool that unlocks doors. In cricket the first two batsmen in are given this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a device that unlocks, and the batsmen who begin a cricket innings are called by the same word.

clue.text: Deal with a character fault

indicators.note: the first piece comes with the second held inside it, wrapped around

blocks.note: the letter D spelt out as a word
in tennis a let is a faulted serve that clips the net

explanation.surface: Advice on correcting a flaw in someone's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: DEE, the name of a letter, holds LET to give DELETE. Read whole, the clue describes what an editor does when one letter is wrong: strike it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleting removes a wrong letter in a text, which is the way an editor handles a typing error.

clue.text: Fish at Land's End and put on the line as bait

definitions.text: put on the line as bait

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Land
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler fishing at Land's End, the tip of Cornwall, hangs bait on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, but here it means the last letter of Land.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something is to hang it loosely, as an angler suspends bait to tempt a fish.

clue.text: How you know for a fact there's no water shortage?

definitions.text: How you know for a fact

blocks.clueFragment: How you know for a fact
blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for knowing with complete certainty
second meaning: a water source brimming to the top, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for certainty, read literally, describes a brimming water source; 'How you know' is answered by the phrase that follows 'know'.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something full well is to be completely sure of it, and a brimming water source means plenty to drink.

clue.text: Competed, too, but was beaten in the race

definitions.text: Competed, too, but was beaten in the race

blocks.note: too means also
ran as in took part in a race

explanation.surface: A runner took part in the race as well but lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order. Read whole, the clue describes an entrant who ran too but did not win.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or competitor that takes part without finishing among the winners, hence an unsuccessful entrant.

clue.text: Think the lady outside is shaking with laughter

indicators.note: something shaking is jumbled about, so these letters are mixed up
one piece sits outside the other, wrapping around it

blocks.note: taken as written, then mixed
to muse is to think deeply

explanation.surface: Someone considers a woman who is trembling with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' only serves the surface. 'Shaking with laughter' looks like one phrase, but the definition starts at 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something amusedly is to do it in an entertained way, as when laughing at something.

clue.text: Get a whiff going up

blocks.note: taken as written
a whiff is a smell or scent

explanation.surface: Someone catches a smell as they climb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or rise, the act of moving upward.

clue.text: Become positive as you elaborate on the theme

blocks.note: first meaning: what a photographic image does in the darkroom
second meaning: expand an idea or musical theme

explanation.surface: Advice that a speaker grows more confident by expanding on a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: In film photography the exposed film is processed so an image appears, and prints made from negatives are positives.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographic film is processed into a visible image, and a composer expands musical material in the same named process.

clue.text: The attraction of a gun battle?

definitions.note: the answer is the pulling of pistols that starts a gun battle

blocks.note: first meaning: something that pulls in crowds
second meaning: the quick pulling of pistols in a Western shootout

explanation.walkthrough: The answer means both a crowd-pulling attraction and the pulling of a pistol that opens a shootout.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is something that pulls in crowds, and in a Western duel it is the quick pulling of a pistol from its holster.

clue.text: Not all who stray, anyway

indicators.note: letters that stray wander out of their places, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: some is a part rather than all
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrug that only some people wander off, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Somehow means in one way or another, by whatever means, much as anyway can mean regardless of how.

clue.text: Who, me?

definitions.note: an example of the answer, singular
an example of the answer, singular

blocks.note: first example: an interrogative and relative word standing for a person
second example: the object form of the first person

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like an innocent protest, but it simply lists two words of one grammatical class.
explanation.definitionFit: Who and me are both words that stand in place of a noun, the grammatical class used for people and things.

clue.text: He likes to see people tastefully dressed

definitions.text: He likes to see people tastefully dressed

blocks.clueFragment: He likes to see people tastefully dressed
blocks.note: surface reading: a man who admires elegant clothes
setter's reading: dressed as in a dish prepared with seasoning, to be eaten

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' suggests clothing, but salads and crabs are dressed too; the man here wants people prepared for the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats human flesh, so he would want people seasoned and prepared like food served at dinner.

clue.text: Lineage any crest will reveal

indicators.note: the letters reveal something else once rearranged, showing a new word

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms will show where a family comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is the line of forebears from whom someone descends, which is what lineage means.

clue.text: Haggled with, but paid for

blocks.note: first meaning: negotiated
second meaning: bought someone a drink or meal

explanation.surface: Someone bargained hard with a seller, then picked up the bill anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: To treat with someone is an old phrase for negotiating terms with them.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has treated with another has negotiated terms, and one who treats a friend covers the cost of their meal.

clue.text: Butter up the biscuit

blocks.note: first meaning: flatter in a servile way
second meaning: a pale yellowish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Spreading butter on a biscuit at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'butter' and 'biscuit' suggest the kitchen; one is flattery and the other a colour name.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter obsequiously, and fawn and biscuit are both names for a light beige-brown colour shade.

clue.text: One of the less intelligent devices for light control?

definitions.note: the answer is the comparative adjective, less clever
the answer is one such device

blocks.note: first meaning: comparative of an adjective for slow-witted
second meaning: a switch that turns lamps down gradually

explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the' governs both halves: the word is a comparative meaning less clever and also a switch that lowers lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch that lowers brightness gradually takes its name from the word that also means less bright or less clever.

clue.text: Wanders about but doesn't go right into

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, sitting inside it

blocks.note: one who does not go stays
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone roams around but never quite enters a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander away from a path or group, roaming aimlessly about.

clue.text: Get your ear accustomed to a song you're hearing

indicators.note: what you hear is the spoken sound, so the phrase is judged by how it is said

blocks.note: a song is a tune, said with the article

explanation.surface: Advice on learning to appreciate a piece of music you are listening to.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune is to adjust or bring into harmony, as when the ear becomes used to an unfamiliar sound.

clue.text: Where you listen, engrossed, to the gypsy telling your future?

definitions.note: read as two words, 'in tent': inside the fortune-teller's canvas booth

linkWords: to the gypsy telling your future

blocks.note: first meaning: inside the canvas booth of a fairground fortune-teller, completed by the rest of the clue
second meaning: absorbed, giving full attention

explanation.walkthrough: A fairground fortune-teller works in a small canvas booth; split the answer into two words to see where you sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being intent on something means giving it complete attention, which is the state of an engrossed listener.

clue.text: Go on, on cue, holding out the box

indicators.note: the second word holds the others, keeping them inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a tin is a small metal box
taken as written

explanation.surface: A director urging an actor to carry on when the prompt comes, holding a box out.
explanation.walkthrough: CUE holds ON and TIN, giving C-ONTIN-UE.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue is to carry on doing something without stopping, which is what go on means.

clue.text: Only the matron is French

blocks.note: first meaning: nothing more than, simply
second meaning: the French word for mother

explanation.surface: A remark that the only French person present is the hospital matron.
explanation.walkthrough: A matron is a married woman or mother, and French for mother is mère.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child, and in French it is the word for mother.

clue.text: A leisurely drink, doubtless, inside

indicators.note: the earlier words are placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: the drink is slang for the sea, here the Mediterranean, MED
taken as written
being without doubt is being sure

explanation.surface: Someone is certainly enjoying a slow drink indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, and the Med is the Mediterranean; A and SURE go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured pace is slow and deliberate, unhurried, which is what leisurely describes.

clue.text: The fish is fresh trout with a little bread stuffing

indicators.note: a fresh version is newly made, so these letters are arranged anew
only a small piece of the word is used, its opening letter
stuffing goes inside something, so one piece is packed into the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the first letter of bread

explanation.surface: A recipe: fresh trout with a little breadcrumb stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized as food, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Having opposed, is leant on, emerging

indicators.note: one piece emerges from within the other, showing in its middle

blocks.note: to rest on something is to lean on it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who put up opposition has been pressured, yet comes through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having opposed' needs the past participle, as in 'having resisted', so the answer is that form of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resisted is to have fought against or withstood something, so the person has stood in opposition.

clue.text: Join forces with again in all seriousness

blocks.note: first meaning: form an alliance once more
second meaning: truly, genuinely

explanation.surface: A sincere proposal to renew a former partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-ALLY, the word means form an alliance anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Really means truly or genuinely, and read as re-ally it means to become allied once again.
